@Tbl-17-master-synthesis pairs each law with the records that carry it, the premise its evidence cannot always settle, and the restriction that holds while that premise stays open. The numbers each row needs come from the particular machine and its limit records, not from the table.

\Needspace{25\baselineskip}

| Law                            | Part                                                                                             | Records that carry it                                                                                        | Premise the evidence cannot always settle                                                                                   | What restricts operation while it is open                                                                                                         |
|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Irreversibility**            | I (@sec-body, @sec-brain, @sec-nervous)                                                          | Limit records (@sec-body); the proposer's limits (@sec-brain), which enter the handoff record (@sec-nervous) | Each measured limit, such as floor friction, payload, brake onset, or observation age, still holds under present conditions | A speed or force ceiling sized from the credible limit, a lease derived from the stopping budget, and a fallback reachable from the current state |
| **Endogenous data**            | II (@sec-data, @sec-training, @sec-evaluation)                                                   | Demonstration provenance record, policy manifest, evaluation record                                          | The states the machine enters lie inside the target ODD that closed-loop evaluation sampled                                 | Operation confined to the target ODD, with a runtime monitor on every boundary that can be monitored                                              |
| **Proposal is not permission** | III (@sec-perception, @sec-memory, @sec-intent, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement) | Observation contract, belief record, intent lease, trajectory record, enforcement record, placement record   | The permission path sees fresh, distinguishable state and meets its deadline under load                                     | Refusal and the fallback ladder; an expired lease or stale evidence removes permission without waiting for the proposer                           |
| **Evidence bounds authority**  | IV (@sec-intervention, @sec-verification, @sec-release)                                          | Authority record, fault record, release manifest, and the residual-claims register of this chapter           | The premises of the release claim still hold after release                                                                  | A conditional verdict with standing conditions, and a register entry that restricts authority until its closure test passes                       |

: **The four laws and what they leave open**: Each law leads one part of the book and is carried by that part's records. The last two columns name the premise its evidence cannot always settle and the restriction that holds while the premise is open, for a particular machine rather than as a universal hardware floor. {#tbl-17-master-synthesis tbl-colwidths="[14,17,25,22,22]"}

Four decisions keep the restrictions in the table's last column operational. First, preserve each open entry across model updates until a predeclared closure test supplies evidence. Second, keep learned outputs as proposals and maintain an independently validated permission and fallback path whose processor, scheduling period, sensor coverage, and actuator response follow the plant's measured deadlines. Third, use passive limits only where their load path, stroke, wear, and stopping consequences are tested. Fourth, require named engineering and operations owners to sign the release conditions and define the measurements that withdraw authority. Down that column, every law ends the same way, in a restriction that holds until evidence lifts it rather than a guarantee that holds regardless of the evidence.

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-frontier-fallacies-pitfalls}

Some hazards are unobservable through available sensors, and some claims require more exposure than the design can accumulate. Both limits must shape operating authority rather than disappear into an uncalibrated confidence score. Systems engineers must confront four prevalent fallacies and pitfalls that arise when applying machine learning to physical systems:

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↩ The gap between verified models and unmodeled friction challenges the safety cases in @sec-release-safety-cases-claims.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Relying on vision-based perception alone when the physical hazard is observationally indistinguishable.*\index{Pitfall!sensor omniscience}\index{Observational indistinguishability!sensor omniscience}

The mobile manipulator approaches a transparent hydraulic-fluid film that its navigation camera and lidar cannot distinguish from dry concrete, producing observational indistinguishability\index{Observational indistinguishability}. When the wheels enter the film and spin without grip, the slip reveals the changed surface only after the deceleration the stop assumed is gone. An identical pitfall occurs in high-dexterity tactile manipulation: an optical camera observes a robotic gripper holding a glass vial or a slippery deformable workpiece. Because the external boundary remains stationary during the initial stick-slip phase, the vision pipeline reports a stable grasp while Cattaneo-Mindlin partial slip is already shearing the contact interface. When gross slip occurs, the object accelerates downward in free fall, exceeding the camera-to-actuator reaction deadline. A visually clear path says nothing about the friction the admitted speed requires, and a visually static grasp says nothing about shear contact stability. The operating envelope must account for that unobserved condition through defensible speed restrictions or independently validated sensing. The residual-claims register must retain the friction assumption and its containment measure instead of treating missing visual evidence as evidence of traction. Visual clarity is not traction. When environmental hazards are observationally indistinguishable to primary sensors, safety cannot rest on software perception; the architecture must enforce structural containment—derating operating velocity or requiring mechanical proof-tests—until a qualified, independent physical transducer is integrated and validated.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Assuming stator temperature and current measurements are sufficient to detect rotor magnet flux degradation.*\index{Fallacy!commanded current proxy}\index{Actuator!flux degradation}

The rotor-flux row of @tbl-17-detectorless-modes already names this gap. In permanent magnet synchronous motors governed by Field-Oriented Control (FOC), delivered electromagnetic torque is proportional to quadrature current and permanent magnet flux linkage: $\tau = \frac{3}{2} p \lambda_m i_q$ (@sec-body). When excessive thermal exposure, mechanical shock, or high-amplitude demagnetizing stator transients lower the magnet flux linkage $\lambda_m$, the motor drive still reports its commanded quadrature current $i_q$ and the expected Joule heating ($I^2 R$) while the joint delivers proportionally less torque than that current implies. Nominal current is not proof of torque authority: the drive can draw full rated current while the joint is incapable of holding against gravity or delivering certified braking deceleration. Commanded electrical current does not guarantee delivered mechanical torque. Systems engineers must measure joint torque directly or calibrate rotor state periodically against known gravitational or inertial loads, never relying on current-based torque estimates on gravity-loaded or safety-critical axes without an independent holding brake and torque verification path.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Assuming massive cloud simulation can substitute for physical exposure in certifying open-world safety.*\index{Fallacy!infinite simulation}\index{Sim-to-real gap!simulation limits}

A team runs billions of simulated hours in the cloud to bypass the cost of physical exposure. Simulation evidence holds only for the simulator's own model (@sec-evaluation-evidence-regimes), and a simulated floor with the friction of inspected concrete says nothing about a clear film (@sec-evaluation-limits). Physics engines in modern simulators approximate contact dynamics using regularized Linear Complementarity Problem (LCP) solvers or penalty-based spring-damper models. These approximations smooth over the non-smooth Signorini contact conditions, ignore microscopic stick-slip friction transitions, and omit infinite-dimensional non-rigid deformation and thermal wear. Repetition inside that closed mathematical model adds no evidence about the physical entropy it omits, so it cannot validate sim-to-real\index{Sim-to-real gap} fidelity against open-world deployment conditions. Simulation remains useful for logic checks and software regressions, while physical safety claims strictly require empirical measurements or validated operating envelopes on the target physical machine. Billions of simulated miles verify only the simulator's internal model assumptions. Engineers must maintain strict separation between simulation verification (software logic and regressions) and physical evidence (mechanical contact, friction bounds, sensor noise, thermal dissipation), never granting operational release without empirical evidence on target hardware.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Assuming a foundation model with broad semantic reasoning can self-regulate physical safety.*\index{Fallacy!omniscient VLA}\index{Vision-language-action model!omniscient VLA fallacy}

A team deploys an 8-billion or 70-billion parameter Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation model as the primary controller, assuming that because the model exhibits common-sense reasoning and zero-shot task generalization across semantic benchmarks, it possesses an intrinsic understanding of physics that eliminates the need for low-level deterministic safety interlocks. Treating high semantic capability as physical self-awareness is hazardous: an ungrounded neural network has no physical representation of motor back-EMF, inverter bus voltage limits, gear shear stresses, or non-smooth contact discontinuities. Under out-of-distribution physical conditions, the model hallucinates kinematically infeasible trajectories or commands excessive forces while reporting high softmax confidence and near-zero latent entropy. Semantic reasoning across offline tokens does not confer physical grounding under dynamic stress. Systems architectures must treat all learned foundation models as untrusted proposal generators operating strictly above the proposal boundary, enforcing safety exclusively through an independent, deterministic Nervous System permission path executing at $1\text{ kHz}$ or higher with dedicated hardware cutoffs, verified Control Barrier Functions, and physical stopping fallbacks that cannot be bypassed or delayed by the proposal engine.

:::

## Summary {#sec-frontier-summary}

At the causal boundary\index{Causal boundary} (@sec-boundary-causal-boundary), a computational decision becomes part of a continuing, irreversible physical process. The architecture developed throughout this book connects this physical irreversibility to measured budgets, explicit interfaces, independent enforcement\index{Independent enforcement}, and accountable release decisions. Its frontier lies in the premises those mechanisms still depend on but cannot fully observe or verify. On the running machine, the arithmetic of the stopping budget never changed when the oil film appeared, but one of its terms had rested all along on a floor that nothing measured, and irreversibility made that unmeasured term as binding as any measured one. An engineering record must expose such limits and let them restrict operation for as long as the machine runs, not only on the day a release is signed. Engineering embodied intelligence requires knowing when the available evidence is sufficient to act and when it is not.

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Epistemic frontiers and open physical laws"}
* **An open premise restricts authority:** The residual-claims register takes each premise the release manifest left open and gives it a missing observable, a restriction, an owner, and a closure test declared in advance. On the aisle, the friction entry caps any release at its restricted mode on inspected floors until a floor-film detector passes that test.
* **A late detector is only a logger:** A detector protects against a hazard only if its latency fits inside the margin the stop leaves unspent. When safe and hazardous states give identical telemetry until the action deadline, no algorithm separates them in time, and passive compliance\index{Passive compliance}, a restricted envelope, or a second physical channel must carry the claim.
* **Trials cannot reach a rare-hazard rate:** The exposure wall of @sec-evaluation-trial-limits puts a rare-hazard rate beyond any practical failure-free campaign. A shield between proposal and actuation earns credit only for hazard classes it can observe and intercept in time, and its proposal rate, coverage, and common-cause terms each need evidence of their own.
* **Research counts when it closes an entry:** A new sensor, estimator, or proof matters for deployment only when it closes a named register entry by supplying the missing observable, bounding the tail, or checking its own premises at runtime. An entry that nothing can close is resolved by narrowing authority or withholding operation, not by waiting.
* **Every law leaves a premise open:** Irreversibility rests on measured limits that still hold; endogenous data, on a target ODD that covers the states the machine enters; proposal is not permission, on fresh and distinguishable state; and evidence bounds authority, on premises that still hold after release. Authority stops where that evidence does.
:::

Embodied intelligence fundamentally transforms machine learning from an empirical optimization game into a rigorous systems engineering discipline. Across every chapter of this book, the four bedrock laws have demonstrated that no scale of data, parameter depth, or foundation model reasoning can repeal the conservation of momentum, bypass thermal dissipation limits, or guarantee safety across unobserved states. By anchoring learned policies beneath deterministic nervous systems, bounding execution authority strictly to empirically validated evidence, and maintaining an accountable claims register for every unmodeled hazard, systems engineers can safely deploy autonomous machines into an uncertain, friction-bound world without surrendering physical control.

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From physical AI to the systems discipline"}
This book completes an investigation into the full architecture of machine learning systems. Across the systems curriculum, we explored the single machine (mastering the silicon contract\index{Silicon contract}, arithmetic intensity\index{Arithmetic intensity}, memory hierarchies\index{Memory hierarchies}, and local hardware acceleration\index{Hardware acceleration}), distributed fleets (navigating collective communication fabrics, fault tolerance, cluster orchestration, and high-throughput serving infrastructure), and agentic software trajectories (constructing sandboxed execution environments, dynamic context working sets, and deterministic verification harnesses for autonomous multi-step reasoning). Here, machine learning leaves the digital domain to inhabit embodied physical intelligence—where learned foundation models act as unprivileged proposal engines, real-time nervous systems enforce validated operating bounds, and artificial intelligence at last meets the unyielding conservation laws of the physical universe. This work is dedicated to the students, researchers, and systems engineers who take up the challenge of giving machines safe and capable hands in an open physical world.
:::
